input.question: What happens to a person's debt when they are the last person of a family line and die?
input.ground_truth: It doesn't matter if you have family or not, debt cannot be inherited. If you do have debt when you die, your creditors can take from your estate to pay it off. If your estate is not large enough to pay the whole debt, the debt just goes away.

response.prediction: When the last person in a family line dies, their debts do not simply disappear. Instead, the debts become part of their estate, which is the collection of their assets and property at the time of death. If the estate has enough money or property to pay off the debts, the debts are settled from those assets. However, if there are not enough assets to cover the debts, the remaining debts are usually not passed on to anyone else, because there are no heirs to inherit them. In that case, the debts are often forgiven or written off by the creditors, though the exact process can depend on the laws in the person's country or state.
